title: Minimum Size Subarray in Infinite Array
summary: Given an array nums and a target sum, generate an infinite array by repeating nums.
statement: Given an array nums and a target sum, generate an infinite array by repeating nums. Find the shortest subarray in this infinite array whose sum equals the target. If no such subarray exists, return -1.
constraints: nums is nonempty and contains positive integers; target is positive.
Repeat nums infinitely and choose one finite contiguous subarray summing exactly to target.
Return its minimum length, or -1 if no such subarray exists.
hints: Any target decomposes into whole-array sums plus one cyclic remainder window.
Add the length of complete cycles and find the shortest remainder-sum window in two copies using positive-value sliding window.
For target=q*sum+r, return q*n plus the shortest r window; handle r=0 directly.
Every n consecutive infinite-array values sum to one cycle, and positivity makes the two-copy sliding window exhaustive and shrinkable for the residual portion.
editorial: Every n consecutive infinite-array values sum to one cycle, and positivity makes the two-copy sliding window exhaustive and shrinkable for the residual portion.

tests.explanation: The consecutive values two and three form the shortest sum-five subarray.
Across a cycle boundary, three followed by one reaches four in two positions.
